clue.text: Level area with cluster of woods?

definitions.text: Level area with cluster of woods?

parts.words: Level area with cluster of woods?
parts.note: woods are the heavy balls used in the game of bowls, so a flat lawn where they gather is meant, not a forest

explanation.surface: A flat clearing surrounded by a clump of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woods' suggests trees, but in lawn bowls the balls are called woods; the flat, closely mown lawn they are rolled on is where they cluster.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawn for bowls is famously flat and ends up with the players' balls grouped around the jack.

clue.text: Crate rerouted after deliveries go too far

indicators.note: after says the deliveries piece comes before the reworked crate in the answer

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries (balls bowled)

indicators.note: sent by another route, so the letters of crate are taken along a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shipping crate has been sent a different way once the deliveries overshoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' hints at parcels, but in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled; 'rerouted' reworks the crate's letters into REACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to respond more strongly than the situation warrants, i.e. to go too far.

clue.text: Vote to have leader dropped sailors support

indicators.note: in a down answer the leading letter is dropped lower, moving from the top of the word to its foot

parts.note: to vote is to elect
RN is the Royal Navy, hence sailors

explanation.surface: A call for a vote to oust the leader, backed by the sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have leader dropped' moves the first letter of ELECT down to the end, giving LECTE; it is not deleted.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a stand that holds up a book or notes for a reader or speaker, so a support.

clue.text: Heard German's negative figure

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: nein is German for no

explanation.surface: Someone heard a German give a negative number.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a number, and figure is a common word for a numeral.

clue.text: Indicated novel gets rude

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of gets rude are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book's content was pointed out as turning vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To gesture is to signal by a movement, so gestured means pointed out or signalled.

clue.text: Regularly excel with displays for cakes

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals from the word excel

parts.note: to air something is to display it, so airs means displays

explanation.surface: Someone consistently shines with their exhibitions of baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'excel', giving ECL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are long choux pastries filled with cream and iced with chocolate, a kind of cake.

clue.text: They're in the sky some time rising over British isle

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: min is short for minute, a period of time
I is a standard abbreviation for island or isle

explanation.surface: Something rising in the sky over a British island for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MIN upward to NIM in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi are rain clouds (plural of nimbus), which are found in the sky.

clue.text: Type in good club that will supply ID

parts.note: a brand is a type or kind of product
taken as written
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Someone joining a decent club is told the club will provide identification.
explanation.definitionFit: A branding iron burns an owner's mark into livestock, giving each animal its identification.

clue.text: Charlie feels bitter taking in another's curvy shapes

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: taking in means one piece swallows another inside itself

parts.note: to resent something is to feel bitter about it
another's points back to Charlie, giving a second C

explanation.surface: Charlie is jealous when someone else's shapely figure is admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another's' means a second Charlie, so another C goes inside RESENTS ('taking in').
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent is a curved shape like a new moon, so crescents are curving forms.

clue.text: Gave opinion about place and one is praised

indicators.note: about means the opinion word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to comment is to give an opinion
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone remarked on a venue, and one person gets praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the opinion word round the place and one; 'is' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To compliment someone is to express admiration, so complimented means praised.

clue.text: Young creature mostly on back gets weaker

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used all but its final letter

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep

indicators.note: back means the word for on is read backwards

parts.note: re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A young animal that is mostly lying on its back grows feebler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LAMB to LAM; 'back' turns RE (on, as in 're: your letter') to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lame means feeble or unconvincing, as in a lame excuse; lamer is its comparative.

clue.text: Noted rescue ship in sea …

indicators.note: in means the ship piece sits inside the sea piece

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
Noah's Ark rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: Someone recorded a lifeboat out at sea, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to take note of it, so marked can mean noted or observed.

clue.text: … is Scotsman on vessel from Africa?

indicators.note: in an across answer on means the following pieces come after the vessel

parts.note: a tun is a large cask, a vessel for wine or beer
taken as written
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a Scot on board ship who has come from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the definition is by example: Tunisia is one African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisian describes someone from Tunisia, a country in North Africa, so one example of from Africa.

clue.text: Got to know King Cnut: sea, you heard, must withdraw

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

indicators.note: must withdraw means these letters are taken out of the king's name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken for their sound, letters that sound alike

parts.note: sea sounds like the letter C and you like the letter U

explanation.surface: King Cnut learnt, as legend says, that the sea would not obey his command to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea' and 'you' sound like the letters C and U ('heard'); these 'must withdraw' from CNUT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: To have learnt something is to have come to know it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Some brothels in kingdom's capital city

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few houses of ill repute in a nation's chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital of Finland.

clue.text: Awfully huge robin, one close to you

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of huge robin are jumbled

explanation.surface: A terribly large robin perched near you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' reads as an intensifier for 'huge' but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour lives next door or nearby, so is a person close to you.

clue.text: Punish group breaking into places to the north

indicators.note: breaking into means the group piece forces its way inside the other piece
in a down answer going north means reading the word upward, backwards

parts.note: to put something is to place it, so puts means places
a ring is a group, as of criminals

explanation.surface: A gang invading northern territory is to be punished.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to the north' means reading upward, giving STUP; 'breaking into' sets the group inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: To string someone up is to hang them, an informal phrase for severe punishment.

clue.text: Full development of fancy atrium they gutted

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imaginative, so the letters of atrium are rearranged
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving just the outside letters

explanation.surface: An elaborate atrium completed once its interior was stripped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges ATRIUM into MATURI; 'gutted' empties THEY to TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Maturity is the state of being fully grown or developed.

clue.text: Controls and rules not good I start to notice

indicators.note: not means the good letter is left out of the word for rules

parts.note: a monarch reigns, i.e. rules

indicators.note: start to means only the first letter of notice is taken

explanation.surface: Checks and regulations that are bad: I begin to see that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' takes G out of REIGNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or keep in check, as with a horse's reins, so it controls.

clue.text: Mathematician somewhere in Italy heading for Genoa

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy

indicators.note: heading for means just the first letter of Genoa

explanation.surface: An academic travelling in Italy on the way to Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing was the British mathematician who founded computer science and broke wartime codes.

clue.text: Reputable type of milk opened by puritan

indicators.note: opened by means the milk piece is split apart with the puritan inside

parts.note: UHT is ultra-heat-treated, long-life milk
a prig is a self-righteous, puritanical person

explanation.surface: A respectable brand of milk, opened by a strait-laced person.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honest and respectable, so of good reputation.

clue.text: Going west, protest about French road's condition

indicators.note: in an across answer going west means reading right to left, backwards
about means the protest piece wraps around the road piece

parts.note: a sit-in is a form of protest
rue is French for street or road

explanation.surface: A westward march protesting about the state of a French road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the protest round the road, and 'Going west' reads the whole result from right to left, giving SITIRUEN backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuritis is inflammation of a nerve, a medical condition.

clue.text: Remove weapon from some lunar module

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking a gun off part of a moon lander.
explanation.definitionFit: To unarm is to disarm, taking away someone's weapons.

clue.text: Comparatively shrewd one that might have quarrel

definitions.meaning: a quarrel is a square-headed bolt for a crossbow

explanation.surface: A rather sharper person who might pick a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' suggests an argument, but here it is the old word for a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Archer is the comparative of arch (sly), and also a bowman who shoots bolts or arrows.

clue.text: Notice something protruding from bird

definitions.meaning: a ... is a poster or notice, as in stick no ...
a bird's ... is its beak, which sticks out from the head

explanation.surface: A sign about a beak sticking out from a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill means a posted notice and also the beak of a bird.

clue.text: Cross being put in same complex tests

indicators.note: being put in means the cross goes inside the other piece
complex means intricate, so the letters of same are mixed up

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A cross figure appearing in the same intricate tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges SAME to EAMS, and X goes inside after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are examinations, formal tests of knowledge.

clue.text: Declining and becoming sad

parts.note: going can mean becoming, as in going grey
down means sad or low in spirits

explanation.surface: Falling in health and growing low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down means sinking or decreasing, as a price or the sun declines.

clue.text: Controlling my tarpaulin all over the place covering nothing

indicators.note: covering means the jumbled letters wrap around the nothing piece
all over the place means scattered, so the letters of my tarpaulin are mixed

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone's tarpaulin is strewn everywhere, covering nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' scrambles MY TARPAULIN and 'covering' wraps it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Manipulatory means given to manipulating, influencing others by underhand control.
